hook.text: You already use a coding agent. It's sharp for an hour. Then the session ends, and what it learned goes with it.

keel.text: Keelson is the harness that sits under that agent. One small server, on your own machine. No hosted service, and nothing to sign in to.

chat.text: It starts with chat. You talk to your agent through Keelson, in the browser or the terminal.

state.text: And it keeps the state. Conversations, runs, and the memories you approve are saved locally, and your secrets stay in the keychain.

workflows.text: It makes work repeatable. A workflow is a small YAML graph of agent steps, shell steps, and approval gates, run in the same order every time.

providers.text: It doesn't tie you to one model. Claude, Copilot, Codex, or Pi, chosen per chat, or per step.

ways.text: There are three ways in. The browser, the keelson command line for your shell and scripts, and MCP, so the agent you already use can drive it too.

access.text: Over MCP, you decide how much it can do. Read only, or full control, with a token when you want one.

standalone.text: That's the keel, and it's useful on its own.

ribs.text: When you need more, you raise ribs. A rib is a package that adds tools, workflows, and whole new screens, without forking the harness.

reveal.text: One backbone, many ribs. Every other figure in this series builds on this frame.
